items.title: 5 new openings at this popular shopping centre in Mississauga
items.summary: We’re more than halfway through 2026, and Mississauga’s Heartland Town Centre has already seen a ton of exciting new openings this year. From Japanese ramen and premium leather goods to a sprawling new indoor playground, Heartland Town Centre at Mavis and Brittania has seen a variety of exciting arrivals, with even more slated to open before the year is through. Here’s what opened at HTC during first half of 2026: The iconic Canadian leather brand Danier opened at Heartland in March, bringing their selection of premium leather jackets, bags, boots, wallets, and accessories to the popular outdoor shopping centre. Known for their genuine craftsmanship and uncompromising quality, Danier has a reputation of using the most exquisite leathers and materials in their carefully curated collection, designing clothing and accessories so they’re not just stylish but long-lasting. Originally founded in 1972, Danier has been a leader in the Canadian fashion space for over 40 years, and continues to regularly add beautiful new woollens and woven pieces to their collection. This internationally known brand just opened at Heartland recently in June, and it’s where shoppers will find a wide selection of beauty products, home décor, electronics, toys, stationery, and snacks, all at affordable prices. Miniso turns every visit into a playful shopping experience that doesn’t break the bank. With more than 5,000 locations across the world, Miniso is an international phenomenon and has collaborated with major brands including Coca Cola, Marvel, Hello Kitty, Sesame Street, Mickey and Minnie, Pink Panther, We Bare Bears and Beijing’s Palace Museum. There’s nothing like a hot or cold savoury bowl of ramen, and Kinton Ramen is one of the city’s most popular places to get it. Kinton’s authentic ramen is crafted with rich broths, signature noodles, and a variety of fresh toppings delivering bold flavours.

items.title: Tunnelling complete on transit line expansion from Toronto to Mississauga
items.summary: Tunnelling is complete on a transit line expansion from Toronto to Mississauga. 2 kilometres and create a continuous rapid transit line from Scarborough to Mississauga. “The Eglinton Crosstown West Extension will make it faster and easier for thousands of commuters to get where they’re going each day, improve connectivity across the GTA and support thousands of good-paying jobs during construction,” Prabmeet Sarkaria, minister of transportation, said today. 2 kilometres from Mount Dennis Station to Renforth Drive and will operate mainly underground, according to Metrolinx, the government agency that is building the extension. Crews have completed excavating twin 500-metre tunnels from Mount Dennis Station to Jane Street for the eastern underground segment of the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension, the province said. 3 kilometres from Scarlett Road to Renforth Drive, was completed in June 2024. At Jane Street, trains on the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension will run above ground on an elevated guideway to Scarlett Road before transitioning to the western underground portion of the line, which finished tunnelling in 2024. Once complete, the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension will extend Line 5 Eglinton farther west, creating nearly 30 kilometres of rapid transit along Eglinton Avenue, linking Scarborough, Midtown Toronto and Mississauga into a single continuous transit line.

items.title: Burger chain restaurant to replace Popular Pizza in Mississauga
items.summary: A burger chain will replace a Popular Pizza location in Mississauga. Popular Pizza, a franchise established in 1997 with locations across the Greater Toronto Area, will close the Streetsville restaurant at 17 Tannery St. The pizza place has been in the Tannery Street location for over 10 years. Previously, a Pizza City was in the unit. Popular Pizza has mixed reviews on Google. Some praised the service and tasty pizza, while others criticized the flavour of the pies and customer service. The restaurant is marked as permanently closed on Google. Grind Burgers is set to open in the spot, the company announced on Instagram. Founded in 2019, the burger restaurant has locations in Georgetown and Stoney Creek. The chain specializes in smash burgers, made to order using 100 per cent fresh ground chuck beef, Grind Burgers says on its website. A smash burger is created by pressing the ground meat on the skillet, creating a thin patty with lacy, crispy edges. The process maximizes the seared surface for a flavourful crust.

items.title: Peel Highways Brace for 32 Scheduled Closures on Aug. 11
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the province has scheduled 32 separate closures across provincial highways in Peel Region for August 11, 2026. The affected routes include Highway 10, Highway 401, Highway 403, Highway 410, Highway 9 and the Queen Elizabeth Way, the same corridors that carry most commuter and commercial traffic through Mississauga and the surrounding region. Mississauga.com advises drivers to plan their route before heading out given how many highways are affected at once. The outlet's listing does not spell out a reason for this particular round of closures, though its coverage of other recent days has tied similar work to short-term repairs and routine highway maintenance. Anyone driving through Peel this week should build extra time into their trip and watch for detours. Mississauga.com also points readers to a separate closure list for anyone travelling to highways outside Peel Region.

items.title: Mississauga: Gateway to the best of Ontario
items.summary: Since I started visiting Canada from Nigeria, every return journey tells a different story. But each visit to Mississauga feels less like stepping into a foreign city and more like going home or reconnecting with an old friend. Most of the time, I fly KLM, connecting through Schiphol in Amsterdam to Toronto. Canada has 10 provinces and three territories. Ottawa is the capital of the country while Toronto is the vibrant capital city of Ontario – one of the 10 provinces. Canada has a total land mass – excluding lakes and rivers – of approximately 9,093,507 square kilometres. When we include the freshwater lakes and rivers, the country’s geographical area covers about 9,984,670 square kilometres, making Canada the second-largest country in the world by total area after Russia. Beyond its status as Canada’s economic heartbeat, Toronto, just like Lagos, is a sprawling metropolis of distinct neighbourhoods, a globally renowned cultural hub, and massive centre for tech, media and education. The city also reminds me of New York. Mississauga, which is on the western edge of Toronto, has quietly transformed itself into one of Canada’s most vibrant, multicultural and economically significant cities. For many international travellers, Mississauga serves as the first handshake with Canada because it is home to Toronto Pearson International Airport, the country’s busiest gateway. Within 25 minutes of landing, visitors are immersed in a city that seamlessly combines modern urban living with beautiful parks, waterfronts and diverse cultural experiences. ” The twisting architectural design has earned global acclaim and has become the defining symbol of Mississauga. Standing elegantly against the Ontario skyline, these 50-storey and 56-storey towers featuring a curvaceous hourglass design represent the city’s confidence, innovation and modern outlook.

items.title: Police Urged Him to Turn Himself In. A Day Later, This Brampton Man Was in Custody
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police have charged a Brampton man with aggravated assault after a stabbing at a commercial unit near Dixie Road and Aimco Boulevard in Mississauga on Aug. 1. Police say one adult male was stabbed and rushed to a local trauma centre in serious but stable condition, and is expected to recover. Investigators identified the suspect as 32-year-old Gregory Darling of Brampton and publicly urged him to turn himself in. INsauga reports Darling was arrested the following day, Aug. 2, and charged with one count of aggravated assault. He was held for a bail hearing and appeared at the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton. Police are asking anyone with information about the incident to call Peel Regional Police at 905-453-3311, or to contact Crime Stoppers anonymously for a possible $2,000 reward.

items.title: Man, 32, charged in Mississauga nightclub stabbing
items.summary: A man has been arrested in connection with a stabbing that took place outside a Mississauga nightclub during the August long weekend. On Monday, Peel Regional Police provided an update on the case and announced the arrest of 32-year-old Gregory Darling of Brampton. m. on August 1. When they arrived at the scene, police found a man suffering from multiple stab wounds. He was transported to a trauma centre for treatment. Footage from the scene shows what appears to be splatters of blood near the front entrance of Sugar Daddy’s Nite Club. Darling was subsequently arrested the next day and charged with a single count of aggravated assault. He was held for a bail hearing and attended the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton.

items.title: A Wrong-Way Turn on the QEW Turns Fatal for an 83-Year-Old Hanover Woman
items.summary: According to Ontario Provincial Police, an 83-year-old woman from Hanover has died after she drove the wrong way into oncoming traffic on the Queen Elizabeth Way in Mississauga. Mississauga.com reports the crash happened near Erin Mills Parkway on the night of Aug. 7, when the woman's sedan, travelling toward Toronto in the Fort Erie-bound lanes, collided head-on with another vehicle. Police at the scene initially believed both drivers had suffered only minor injuries. According to OPP, the wrong-way driver's injuries were later upgraded to life-threatening, and she died in hospital. Mississauga.com reports the crash remains under investigation. OPP is asking anyone with information or video footage of the incident to call 1-888-310-1122.

items.title: How a New Rapid-Assessment Clinic Diagnosed a Mississauga Mom's Skin Cancer in Two Weeks After Others Missed It
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, Mississauga mother of three Liliya Leheta had her skin cancer symptoms dismissed by dermatologists for nearly two years before a new rapid assessment clinic at Princess Margaret Cancer Centre diagnosed her within two weeks of her referral. The Star reports Leheta first noticed her skin peeling on her chest in March 2023 after a day out with her kids without sunscreen, and later found a small red mole near the centre of her chest that she initially dismissed. Over the following two years, she watched the mole swell, change shape and bleed, all while an earlier referral to a specialist had been declined. In the fall of 2025, Leheta learned about the newly opened rapid assessment centre for skin cancer at Princess Margaret and was seen within two weeks of being referred there. She was diagnosed with basal cell carcinoma, the most common form of skin cancer in Canada, and a surgeon successfully removed the cancerous tissue less than two months later. The Star reports Leheta remains cancer-free today.

items.title: City of Mississauga warns about event falsely using City name and community centre
items.summary: Residents and businesses are advised to verify event details before registering or purchasing tickets. The City of Mississauga became aware of two Eventbrite listings for the International Conference on Leadership, Innovation, Global Investment, & Professional Development (ICLIGP). The listings falsely claim to be in partnership with the City and state the event will take place at Malton Community Centre from August 31 to September 2, 2026 and November 30, 2026. The City is not affiliated with these events, and no booking exists for this at any City facility. Online promotions for these events have falsely used the City’s name and branding authorization. ca 905-615-3200, ext.
